accent.purpose: The takeaway line and links. Never a status, a fill or a heading.

accent-solid.purpose: The 2px focus outline on buttons, the scenario switch and checklist rows.

pass.purpose: Letters for passed, agreed, approved, shipped and landed.

pass-solid.purpose: Discs, connectors, ring bars, the checklist meter, progress when complete, checked boxes.

pass-tint.purpose: Fill of pass chips, stage marks and the completed checklist head.

pass-line.purpose: Border of pass chips, stage marks and pill rows.

merge.purpose: The one filled action: Approve on the release board and the Merge pull request button.

hold.purpose: Letters for in progress, awaiting approval, held and suspect (Pass*).

hold-solid.purpose: Hold discs and the review loop return path.

spin.purpose: Only the rotating arcs of work in progress and the progress bar while a run is underway.

hold-tint.purpose: Fill of hold chips, hold and active stage marks, the warning row and the running state pill.

hold-line.purpose: Border of hold chips and stage marks; top rule of the warning row.

back.purpose: Letters for failures, errors, incidents, the health gate label and rollbacks.

back-solid.purpose: Fail and rollback discs, the dashed health gate and its trip dot.

back-tint.purpose: Fill of rollback and incident marks, the regret cues and the row flash.

back-line.purpose: Border of rollback and incident marks and the regret cues.

agent.purpose: Authorship, not state: the Agent chip, the bot glyph, the AI-0142 loop token.

agent-tint.purpose: Fill of the Agent chip and the bot disc.

agent-line.purpose: Border of the Agent chip, the bot disc and the loop token.

canvas.purpose: Every slide's ground; deck.js also paints the page in it so transitions never flash black.

canvas-wash.purpose: A radial ellipse from the top-right corner, faded into the canvas by 72%.

surface.purpose: Panels, cards, actor boxes, the check run, default buttons.

subtle.purpose: Panel head bars, neutral chips, the board bar, table header rows, disabled buttons.

well.purpose: Recessed ground: board lanes, counts, the switch track, the state pill at rest.

avatar-tint.purpose: Behind the speaker's avatar and the bio portrait.

line-soft.purpose: Row dividers and head-bar bottoms inside panels.

line-strong.purpose: Bullets, hollow rings, arrows, checkbox borders and gutter line numbers; 3:1, never reading text (disabled labels aside).

ink-2.purpose: Meta, captions, IDs, column headers and the footer.

display.purpose: The cover title (two lines, left column). Closing slides scale the same cut to 96px and 64px.

headline.purpose: One claim per content slide, max 1080px wide, balanced wrapping.

takeaway.purpose: The one closing line of an argument slide, in Takeaway Blue (Ink on the release board).

body.purpose: The theme's base for un-classed slides; the byline name and the check run title sit at this size in bold.

body-side.purpose: Prose beside a panel or under the board lanes.

title.purpose: Terms, row titles, change titles, timeline steps, table row heads.

row.purpose: Definitions and list rows inside panels.

panel-head.purpose: The head bar of every panel; the name inside it at 650.

meta.purpose: Lane names, check names, counts and the pill rows under a slide.

label.purpose: Chips, buttons, switch options and board marks.

caption.purpose: Step, actor, timeline and table notes; exposure lines and ring subtitles use 450, the illustrative label and board foot 500.

id.purpose: Change IDs such as AI-0142 and PR-0161.

code.purpose: Inline code, file names, paths and commands.

chrome.purpose: The footer; the page number is Monaspace Neon 400 at the same size.

shadows.name: panel
shadows.purpose: Panels, actor boxes, change cards and the loop token.

shadows.name: lift
shadows.purpose: The cover's check run and the Questions photo only.

shadows.name: selected-segment
shadows.purpose: The selected option in the scenario switch.

shadows.name: hollow-ring
shadows.purpose: Queued status discs and lane dots the change hasn't reached.

shadows.name: badge-cutout
shadows.purpose: Separates a check badge from the avatar it sits on.

motion.name: settle-budget
motion.purpose: Every effect plays once on the live audience slide (section.sw-live) inside prefers-reduced-motion: no-preference, fills backwards from a visible default, and has finished by 4.95s.

motion.name: ease
motion.purpose: Arrivals: rise, write, focus, grow, draw, reveal, the takeaway.

motion.name: ease-pop
motion.purpose: Results that pop: disc settle, chips, badges, checked boxes.

motion.name: status-settle
motion.value: spin 640ms linear ending at --t; settle 420ms ease-pop at --t; glyph tick 320ms ease at --t + 90ms
motion.purpose: The signature beat: a check queues, spins amber, then settles green (or amber, or red).

motion.name: takeaway
motion.purpose: The takeaway enters only after the slide's moment completes.

motion.name: write
motion.value: clip-path wipe left to right, 360-560ms ease
motion.purpose: Text being written: definitions, states, file lines.

motion.name: focus
motion.value: blur(12px) and translateY(14px) to sharp, 800-900ms ease

motion.name: pop
motion.purpose: Chips, badges, pill rows and checked boxes.

motion.name: draw
motion.value: stroke-dashoffset 1 to 0 on pathLength 1; 600ms arrows, 1500ms error line
motion.purpose: Review-loop arrows and the error-rate line.

motion.name: count
motion.purpose: Queue counts ticking up at different rates.

motion.name: transient
motion.value: visible during the moment, hidden at the end; 3900-3950ms linear
motion.purpose: Live-only in-progress text that gives way to the authored final state.

motion.name: nudge
motion.purpose: A control waiting on the speaker: Run when idle, Approve at the gate.

motion.name: flash
motion.purpose: A board row that rolls back or becomes an incident.

motion.name: spin-loop
motion.purpose: The only infinite animation: the board's active stage while a speaker-started run is going.

motion.name: transition-lift
motion.value: 620ms; incoming rises 22px and fades in, outgoing gone by 60%

motion.name: transition-handoff
motion.value: 900ms cross-fade; incoming waits to 45%, outgoing gone by 40%; view-transition-name sw-hero
motion.purpose: Slides 6 to 8, so the AI-0142 change card moves column to column.

motion.name: reduced-motion-and-print
motion.value: no animation; view-transition-name none; checklist meter transition none
motion.purpose: Static views show the complete authored slide.

components.html:
If you can't explain the diff out loud, you can't approve it.

One landed. One held before anyone saw it. One rolled back after reaching 1%.

Fictional changes, illustrative only

narrative.overview:
There is no governing metaphor, and the North Star says so on purpose. Every picture in the deck is a piece of release tooling the audience already trusts: a check run, a pull-request queue, a project board, an instructions file, a deployment timeline, a checklist. Each is redrawn crisp and large for a 1280×720 slide. The talk argues that a change needs evidence before it ships, so the illustrations are the evidence surfaces themselves. The deck refuses costume worlds and the dark neon AI deck.

The material is a light product UI, enlarged for a room. A cool off-white canvas carries a faint blue wash from the top-right corner. White panels have hairline borders and soft, ink-tinted offset shadows. Mona Sans sets every word, and Monaspace Neon appears only where the audience reads a literal string. Color stays neutral until something has a state: four status hues with fixed meanings, each paired with a glyph, and one blue saved for the slide's takeaway, links and focus. Density is GitHub-scale (rows, chips, counts, IDs), but every size is lifted for the back of the room.

Each slide has one authored moment: the cover's checks turning green, two queues filling at different rates, three checks failing, a file written line by line, one more check on each board slide, a review loop that ends in a merge box, an error line crossing the health gate, a table filling, a checklist cascade. The finished state is the markup. Motion only replays how the slide got there, once, on the live audience slide. It uses two easings: `cubic-bezier(0.16, 1, 0.3, 1)` for arrivals and an overshooting `cubic-bezier(0.34, 1.56, 0.64, 1)` for results that pop.
keyCharacteristics: Cool off-white canvas, white hairline panels, soft offset shadows; panels never nest.
Mona Sans throughout, in a slightly widened heavy cut for headings; Monaspace Neon only for literal strings.
Four status hues with fixed meanings, each paired with a glyph; one blue for takeaways, links and focus.
Pills report state, circles report checks, and rounded rectangles are controls or literal tokens.
One authored moment per slide, played once and settled by 4.95s; the static slide is already complete.
Simulated material is labeled illustrative on the slide itself.

rules.name: The Complete Without Motion Rule
rules.body: The authored markup is the finished slide; motion only replays the path to it. deck.js adds `sw-live` to a slide only in the audience window, while that slide is active, the page is visible and not printing, and no reduced-motion preference is set. Every effect sits inside `prefers-reduced-motion: no-preference`, fills `backwards` from a visible default, and settles by 4.95s (the review slide is the longest). The one infinite animation is the release board's stage spinner while a speaker-started run is going.

rules.name: The Static Twin Rule
rules.body: Anything that only makes sense live has a static twin. `.sw-static` shows until its section is `data-enhanced="true"`, and `.sw-dynamic` only after. `.live-only` text stays hidden and appears only inside a finite `transient` animation. Print turns off all animation and transitions and hides dynamic twins and board controls. The release board's authored markup is its PDF snapshot, and the script restores it whenever the slide leaves the audience view.

rules.name: The Illustrative Label Rule
rules.body: Every simulated change, count, rate or board says so on the slide in an 18px Secondary Ink line ("Fictional change, illustrative only", "Illustrative: seven drafted and two shipped is not measured data"), never only in the speaker notes.

rules.name: The Fixed Meaning Rule
rules.body: A status hue means one thing everywhere: on chips, status discs, board marks, timeline outcomes and the colored words of a takeaway. Green is passed, amber is in progress or held, red is failed or rolled back, violet is an agent. A landed or merged change is green, never GitHub's purple, because violet already means agent. No hue carries a status alone: a glyph (check, pause, undo, x, bot, person) or the word itself says the same thing.

rules.name: The Ink and Solid Rule
rules.body: Letters use a family's ink step. Discs, bars, connectors and strokes use its solid step. Chips sit on the tint with the line as their border. Never set text in a solid or fill a disc with an ink.

rules.name: The One Blue Rule
rules.body: The accent is the takeaway, the link and the focus ring. It never marks a status, fills a surface or colors a heading. Brand marks are not the accent: the contact icons keep their own brand colors.

rules.name: The Mono Means Literal Rule
rules.body: Monaspace Neon sets only what the audience would type or search for: change IDs, file names, paths, commands, inline code, the file's line numbers and the page number. Headings, labels, column heads and prose are Mona Sans.

rules.name: The Floor Rule
rules.body: At 1280×720, argument text (bullets, side notes, definitions, step names) is 22px or larger. Panel UI text sits at 19–21px: panel heads, table cells, the board console, panel footers and the source note under a table. Labels and captions never go below 18px, and the footer and page number are 17px chrome. Known exceptions, not precedents: the Agent and Human chips inside release-board rows (16px), the change IDs in those rows and in the comparison line (17px), and the moving AI-0142 token (17px mono).

rules.name: The Bundled Type Rule
rules.body: Both families ship beside the deck (`slides/assets/fonts/`, OFL-1.1) with `font-display: block`, and deck.js loads every face before the first transition, so a slide never captures invisible or fallback text.

rules.name: The 72px Margin Rule
rules.body: Everything that anchors to an edge anchors to the 72px margin: the footer, the page number, the takeaway, positioned panels and the release board's static comparison line.

rules.name: The One Takeaway Rule
rules.body: An argument slide ends with at most one takeaway line, pinned 82px from the bottom, entering only after the slide's moment completes (each slide sets its own `--td`). On the release board the takeaway is the outcome sentence: it's set in Ink with each outcome word in its status ink, and it appears only when a run completes.

rules.name: The One Surface Rule
rules.body: Panels never nest. Inside a panel, structure is a head bar, a Soft Hairline or a tinted footer row. A white card may sit in a gray well (the change card in its lane), never in another panel.

rules.name: The Lift Is for Heroes Rule
rules.body: Only the cover's check run and the Questions photo take the Lift shadow. Everything else that floats takes the Panel shadow.

rules.name: The Pill Means State Rule
rules.body: A pill reports a state; a rounded rectangle is something you press or a literal string. Buttons, the scenario switch, the merge button and the AI-0142 token are rectangles; chips, counts, stage marks and outcome rows are pills.

rules.name: The Circle Means a Check Rule
rules.body: A circle is a check's state. It's filled with a white glyph when done, a hollow ring when queued, a dashed ring when drafted, amber arcs while running, and the person's face with a green badge when a person approved. Checklist boxes are rounded squares because the speaker ticks them.

dos: Do draw each argument as the tool that proves it (a check run, a pull-request queue, a board, an instructions file, a deploy timeline, a checklist), built from panels, chips and status discs.
Do give every status its fixed hue and its glyph: check for pass, pause for hold, undo for rollback, x for failure or incident, bot for agent, person for human.
Do set status words in the ink step and draw discs, bars, connectors and strokes in the solid step.
Do end an argument slide with one Takeaway line, 82px from the bottom, entering only after the slide's moment (`--td`).
Do author the finished state in markup and let motion replay the path to it: `backwards` fills, gated on `section.sw-live` and `prefers-reduced-motion: no-preference`, settled by 4.95s.
Do give anything live-only a static twin (`.sw-static` / `.sw-dynamic`, or `.live-only` revealed by a finite `transient`) so the PDF, presenter, reduced-motion and no-script views read complete.
Do label every simulated change, count, rate and board on the slide itself, in an 18px Secondary Ink line.
Do show a person's approval as their avatar with a green check badge, and an agent's work with the violet bot and the Agent chip.
Do keep a 2px Focus Blue outline on every control (2px outside buttons and switch options, 3px inside checklist rows), and let arrow keys and clickers advance the deck from a focused control.
Do keep the bio and Thank You contact blocks exactly as authored, including the Font Awesome icons in their brand colors and the struck-through Twitter line in Secondary Ink.
donts: Don't use Takeaway Blue or Focus Blue for a status, a fill or a heading.
Don't spend a status hue on decoration or a second meaning; a landed or merged change is green, never purple, because violet means agent.
Don't nest a panel in a panel, or give anything but the cover's check run and the Questions photo the Lift shadow.
Don't set prose, headings or labels in Monaspace Neon.
Don't set argument text below 22px or labels below 18px; the board rows' 16px chips, their 17px IDs and the 17px loop token are exceptions, not precedents.
Don't shape a button as a pill or a status chip as a rectangle.
Don't add looping or autoplaying motion; the board's stage spinner is the only infinite animation, and it runs only after the speaker presses Run.
Don't add colored or blurred glows or tinted shadows; shadows are Ink at low alpha, and the only colored halo is the zero-blur nudge on a control waiting for the speaker.
Don't dress the deck in a costume world or the dark neon AI look; the release tooling is the only illustration.
Don't present a number, chart or change as real; nothing on a slide is connected to a real model, repository, pipeline or production traffic.
